**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the prior holder until the replacement succeeds**

When an alert ID is retried after its acknowledgement failed, this immediately transfers the prior notification and retires its holder before `n.show()` has succeeded. If the replacement then throws or emits `failed` before replacing the delivered OS item, the catch/failed path calls `release()`, so the still-visible earlier notification remains in Notification Center but its click handler now targets an `over` entry and opens nothing. Keep the earlier holder active until the replacement is confirmed, or restore it on replacement failure.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exercise the restored-object path on real macOS**

This model injects the exact unverified premise the fix depends on—that `getHistory()` creates a competing entry which receives the click—so it passes even if Electron/macOS still drops Notification Center clicks. The existing attended test at `notifications-os.desktop.real.spec.ts:281` permits clicking either the banner or Notification Center and does not wait for the banner to disappear, so it can pass without exercising this regression. Update that native scenario to wait for the banner to leave, click the retained Notification Center item, and require `alert-clicked` before treating this behavior as covered.

Addressed in 1088447bbeaac88259788da46db7d635fe54662a with a separate attended case in this PR's own suite, `okr/desktop/e2e/alerts.e2e.mjs`: "installed (TXE-4684): a Flow alert clicked in Notification Center after its banner left opens the supporting task". The NC-owned `notifications-os.desktop.real.spec.ts` is left unchanged.

What the case does:
- It is a hand run on macOS (`OKR_E2E_NC_LATE=1`, `OKR_E2E_GATE_DIR`), on a run-owned test package against a real keycloak-mode okr-api.
- It fails before anyone is asked anything if macOS refuses the package notification permission (from Electron's own log).
- READY 1 / `go-1`: it causes one alert, then requires Electron's `Notification restored (<id>)`, the restored entry this fix is about, in the unmodified build.
- READY 2 / `banner-gone`: written only on the person's word that the banner has left. An elapsed time proves nothing, because a banner can be set to stay.
- Then one Notification Center click, in its own 5-minute window. The case requires all of: `alert-clicked` for that id with `sameSession`, the task's route and region, and usernoted's `Received response` for that request id.

The actual OS run is still pending. It is the PR's explicit acceptance hold, and the PR does not merge before it passes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset gate markers before waiting**

When this attended case is rerun with the same `OKR_E2E_GATE_DIR`, the prior `go-1` and `banner-gone` files still exist, so both gates open immediately and the test no longer establishes that the current banner has left before prompting for the click. This can turn a required retry into apparent Notification Center evidence even though the intended late-click condition was skipped; remove each marker before announcing its gate or require a fresh run-specific directory.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Select the alert created by this attended run**

If a previous failed/interrupted run left any `flow_support` alert pending for this reused real account, it can be fetched after sign-in and this unqualified `find` permanently chooses that older alert instead of the one just created by `supportAs`. The subsequent click assertion and route assertion then refer to different alerts, making the required retry fail despite correct behavior; snapshot the received events before creating the support and select only the new event (or otherwise correlate it to the created support).

Fixed in 10226f7d43300e3888705ea1cf405232b3277d26: the case fails at once if `go-1` or `banner-gone` already exists in `OKR_E2E_GATE_DIR` (an earlier run's), naming the file and asking for a fresh gate directory, before the app is launched. A rerun therefore cannot reuse a gate.

Fixed in 10226f7d43300e3888705ea1cf405232b3277d26.

- Before go-1, the case lets anything the account had pending arrive (3 alert intervals) and records the ids received so far.
- After the support is written, the run's alert is the one `flow_support` alert received since then that is not among those ids (`newAlerts` in `e2e/fixtures/click-proof.mjs`, unit-tested in `test/click-proof.test.cjs`).
- Any count other than exactly one fails before the person is asked to click, rather than choosing.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Capture usernoted before an app-click timeout aborts**

When the regression under test occurs—macOS records the Notification Center response but Electron never emits `alert-clicked`—the assertion at line 692 throws before this command runs. Consequently `usernoted` remains empty, and `keepEvidence` omits `nc-late-usernoted.log`, losing the OS-side evidence needed to distinguish the target bug from a click that never reached macOS. Capture the filtered unified log in `finally` once `alertId` and `shownAt` are known so failed runs retain the required evidence too.

Fixed in f4bb42900bead44ff7365e4c3a9f249a5df80012.

- `alertId` and `shownAt` are kept outside the `try`. Once the alert is shown, `finally` reads usernoted's lines for its request id (`process == "usernoted" AND eventMessage CONTAINS <id>`, from 2 s before it was shown) whatever happened: presented, any `Received response`, `Bringing app`. These are written to `nc-late-usernoted.log`.
- So a run that fails on `alert-clicked` still keeps the OS-side record that tells a click lost in the app from one that never reached macOS.
- A failure to read the log fails the run as evidence not kept.
- The post-click assertion still reads its own `Received response` query.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correlate the alert instead of using a fixed drain delay**

When the reused real account has more than a few pending alerts, this six-second wait cannot ensure they have all arrived before `before` is captured: this test configures one-second spacing, while `MaxAlertsPerFetch` is one and the server can retain up to 100 undecided candidates. An older `flow_support` first delivered after the snapshot is therefore treated by `newAlerts` as belonging to this run, causing the exactly-one assertion to fail despite correct notification behavior. Fresh evidence beyond the prior comment is the server's explicit one-alert-per-fetch and 100-candidate bounds, which show that three intervals are not a drain guarantee; correlate the alert with the created support or use state owned by this run.

Fixed in 5069a9758ded8748020f0d82e1ab844cab3dcede.

- The fixed 3-interval settle is replaced: the case waits until no alert has arrived for 5 intervals, up to 4 minutes (`drained()` in `e2e/fixtures/click-proof.mjs`, unit-tested).
- It fails plainly if the account's backlog never stops arriving.
- Only then does it record the ids received so far and hold at READY 1. A backlog handed out one per fetch is therefore fully in `before` before this run causes its alert.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the owner's alert preferences after the attended run**

When this attended case runs against the reusable `FLOW_OWNER` account, `ownerTask` permanently sets `quiet_hours.enabled` to false, and the `finally` block only stops the app. A successful or failed run therefore changes shared account state and can alter later notification tests; snapshot the original preferences and restore them—including the previously-unsaved state—in `finally`.

Fixed in 946a0ff29897ba52663cf0eec7e26f8c38cb0e77.

- `ownerTask` now returns the preferences it found.
- Both installed Flow cases (TXE-4402's and this one) write them back in `finally`, before the app closes, with `If-Match` at the saved row's version (`restorePrefs`).
- A run that passed fails if they cannot be put back.
- Limit: the API has GET and PUT only (`okr/internal/httpapi/alerts.go:27-28`), so a row the owner had never saved cannot return to unsaved. It comes back as the same values, saved, and later alerts behave the same.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore preferences when owner setup fails**

If either focus/task request or the status assertion fails after the preference PUT, `ownerTask` throws before returning `prior`, so both callers leave `mine` null and their `finally` blocks skip `restorePrefs`; the reusable `FLOW_OWNER` account is then left with quiet hours disabled. Fresh evidence after the cleanup change is that restoration is registered only after this second `page.evaluate` completes; capture the snapshot before mutating or restore internally on setup failure.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L150-L156](https://github.com/txehq/txe/blob/946a0ff29897ba52663cf0eec7e26f8c38cb0e77/AGENTS.md#L150-L156)

Fixed in 65cb56b94b34c7e3dd77e34c087d2af14e794d14: `ownerTask` now does the focus and task setup (`ownerFocusTask`) inside a `try`. If that fails after the preferences were changed, it puts them back (`restorePrefs`) and then rethrows the setup's own error. A failure to restore is logged, not allowed to replace that error.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear omitted artifacts before writing evidence**

When an attended retry reuses `OKR_E2E_EVIDENCE_DIR` and the current run fails before creating the events file or collecting `usernoted`, these conditional writes leave the prior run's corresponding files in place while `keepEvidence` reports success. The resulting directory can mix the current Electron log with stale click evidence and misdiagnose the regression; remove optional artifacts first, write empty current files, or require a fresh output directory.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Surface restoration failures after a failed attended run**

When this attended case has already failed and the subsequent preference PUT also fails, the `restoreError && !runError` condition silently discards the cleanup failure; the TXE-4684 case has the same behavior unless evidence keeping also failed. This can leave the reusable `FLOW_OWNER` account mutated while the reported error gives no indication that later runs now start from contaminated shared state, so preserve both failures with an aggregate error or at least report the restoration failure unconditionally.

Fixed in d3025fd29d8a34d0a65f39fda2850bc94c760f5d.

- The case now requires `OKR_E2E_EVIDENCE_DIR` to be fresh (not there yet, or empty) before launch (`freshDir`).
- `keepEvidence` writes all three files every time, each empty where the run got no further.
- So a retry can never mix its files with an earlier run's.

Fixed in d3025fd29d8a34d0a65f39fda2850bc94c760f5d.

- Both installed cases now report every cleanup failure through `cleanupOutcome` (in `e2e/fixtures/click-proof.mjs`, unit-tested).
- A cleanup failure alone fails a run that passed.
- With a failed run, it is joined to the run's own error in an `AggregateError`, so a preferences restore that fails after a failed run is always reported.
